channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Vídeo: Sabatina de Jorge Messias é marcada para 29 de abril
item.description: The sabatina (hearing) for Jorge Messias, nominated by President Lula to the Supreme Federal Court (STF), is scheduled for April 29 in the Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ), with a plenary vote expected the same day. Senator Weverton (PDT-MA) is the rapporteur of the nomination. Although announced in 2025, the name was formally submitted to the Senate only last week.

item.title: Seguro-defeso: Câmara rejeita mudança feita pelo Senado e texto vai à sanção
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies rejected the Senate's amendments to Bill PLV 1/2026, preserving the original text by Senator Beto Faro (PT-PA) on the fisheries unemployment insurance (seguro-defeso). The bill, headed for presidential sanction, sets new registration and identification rules to prevent fraud, allows settlement of pending installments in 2026 if eligibility criteria are met, and excludes arrears payments from the budget ceiling under Law 10.779/03. For 2026, the total allocated for seguro-defeso, excluding arrears, is R$ 7.9 billion.

item.title: STF tem 4 a 1 por eleição indireta no Rio e julgamento é suspenso por pedido de vista
item.description: The Federal Supreme Court formed a 4-1 majority in favor of indirect election for the interim government mandate in Rio de Janeiro, with ministers André Mendonça, Kassio Nunes Marques and Cármen Lúcia supporting the prevailing position. The session was suspended following a request for review by Minister Flávio Dino, halting the judgment before its conclusion.

item.title: O lado do juiz
item.description: Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça received a high honor from the São Paulo Legislative Assembly for his work in investigations involving the defunct Banco Master and improper deductions from retirees' payments. He is viewed as a hope by the opposition to President Lula, despite claiming that money should not be the goal in legal careers. Mendonça is expanding his educational business through the Iter institute, raising concerns about potential conflicts of interest.

item.title: Só vale para Bolsonaro?
item.description: PT lawmakers urged the STF to extend house arrest to all elderly or seriously ill prisoners, criticizing the privileged treatment given to Jair Bolsonaro, who received care in a luxury private hospital. The collective habeas corpus notes that tens of thousands of inmates with worse health conditions remain in overcrowded, unsanitary prisons, where disease-related mortality is alarmingly high. The case is under the rapporteurship of Minister André Mendonça, appointed by Bolsonaro.

item.title: Por justiça tributária
item.description: The Ministry of Finance announced the inclusion of the race/color question in the Income Tax declaration starting in 2026, meeting a historical demand from Brazil's Black movement for statistical visibility. This measure, the result of decades of mobilization such as the campaign 'Do not let your color go blank,' will enable analyses of how the tax burden differently affects racial groups and support fairer fiscal policies. The initiative is seen as an advancement in the fight against racial discrimination and in building effective public policies based on data.

item.title: Poder de dissuasão
item.description: Following the U.S. invasion of Venezuela, the Lula government plans to double defense spending under pressure from the Armed Forces. Defense Minister José Múcio Monteiro confirmed the approval of a legislative measure to exclude R$ 5 billion annually from the fiscal target through 2031 to fund military modernization, including Gripen jets and a nuclear-powered submarine. The three branches of the Armed Forces have submitted an R$ 800 billion investment plan over 15 years, prioritizing the Navy, Air Force, and Army.

item.title: Devemos abrir os olhos
item.description: Afonsinho Médico's column analyzes the new CBF management under Samir Xaud, highlighting promising initiatives such as the proposal for a single league, tackling the disorganized calendar, and the need for financial fair play. It points to structural challenges like the revenue-sharing deadlock from broadcast rights locked until 2029/2030, the excess of foreign players in the Brasileirão (9 per match), and lack of pitch standardization. The column concludes that club unity — exemplified by statements from Pedrinho (Vasco) and Leila Pereira (Palmeiras) — is essential to overcome Brazil's football lag behind European leagues.

item.title: Robert Crumb contra Trump
item.description: The newly released Brazilian book 'Tempos Modernos' compiles works by Robert Crumb, his wife Aline Kominsky-Crumb, and daughter Sophie Crumb from 2017 to 2021. The collection uses satire and irony to explore Crumb’s fixation on Trump’s hair and habits, anticipating his criticism of the former president long before his political rise. A highlight is the 1989 comic 'Point The Finger,' where Crumb suggests putting Trump’s head in a toilet, revealing a prophetic view of Trump as a threat to civilization.

item.title: Sabatina de Jorge Messias é marcada para 29/4; relator será o senador Weverton Rocha
item.description: The president of the Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee, Otto Alencar, scheduled Jorge Messias' confirmation hearing for April 29. Senator Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA) will serve as rapporteur and has already signaled support, stating Messias meets the necessary qualifications for the Supreme Court. Despite delays in transmitting the nomination due to tensions between the Presidency and the Senate, analysts believe Messias has sufficient support for approval.

item.title: Congresso vota em 30 de abril veto de Lula a PL da Dosimetria
item.description: The National Congress is scheduled to vote on April 30 on President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's full veto of the Dosimetria Bill, which seeks to reduce sentences for those convicted of antidemocratic acts, including the January 8, 2023 attacks. The bill, approved in December, would apply the single most severe penalty when crimes against the democratic state and coup attempts occur in the same context, rather than summing penalties, and would speed up prison regime progression. Lula vetoed the bill, arguing defendants received fair trials with solid evidence, and that the measure would benefit figures such as Bolsonaro and former ministers of his administration.

item.title: Haddad admite conversas com representante do agro, mas diz que ‘não há pressa’ para definir chapa
item.description: Fernando Haddad confirmed he has been in talks with Teresa Vendramini (Teca), former president of the Brazilian Rural Society and now affiliated with the PDT, about a potential vice-presidential spot on his 2026 São Paulo gubernatorial ticket. He praised her as a progressive leader in modern, environmentally responsible agribusiness and emphasized her potential to strengthen the Workers’ Party’s presence in the state’s interior. Haddad said there is no rush to finalize the ticket and also named Márcio França, Marina Silva, and Simone Tebet as possible coalition partners.

item.title: Davi convoca sessão do Congresso para analisar veto à dosimetria
item.description: Congress President Davi Alcolumbre has called a session for April 30 to review President Lula’s total veto of Bill PL 2.162/2023, which proposed sentence reductions (dosimetry) for non-leaders and non-financiers of the January 8, 2023 anti-democratic attacks. Lula vetoed the bill citing unconstitutionality and threat to the legal order, while senators Jorge Seif and Esperidião Amin support overturning the veto, and Rogério Carvalho (PT-SE) opposes it, labeling the acts as heinous crimes.

item.title: “Me desculpei por não ter parabenizado pela indicação”, diz Leite sobre Caiado
item.description: Governor Eduardo Leite (PSD-RS) apologized for not congratulating Ronaldo Caiado (PSD-GO) on his designation as the party's pre-candidate for president, calling the omission an 'unintentional indiscretion'. Despite the apology, Leite reiterated that he maintains political disagreements with Caiado.

item.title: Lula sanciona lei que cria crime de 'vicaricídio' e amplia pena para violência contra mulher
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed a law establishing the crime of 'vicaricide' — the killing of children or stepchildren to punish the mother — and increased penalties for violence against women. The package also includes mandatory electronic ankle monitors for aggressors in domestic violence cases, as part of a broader effort to strengthen victim protection.

item.title: Lula recebe marcha das centrais sindicais em 15 de abril
item.description: Trade union centrals are holding the Workers' Class March on April 15 in Brasília, starting at 8 a.m., followed by an afternoon meeting with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The march aims to pressure for labor rights advances, professional valorization, an end to the 6X1 work schedule, and approval of the 2026/2030 workers' agenda with 68 items, including app-based work regulation and combating unrestricted pejotization.

item.title: Ministros do STF citam milícias e crise institucional ao julgar regras para eleição no Rio
item.description: STF ministers emphasized the institutional crisis and militia presence in Rio de Janeiro during the ruling on rules for the state’s interim government election, following the resignation of former Governor Cláudio Castro. Gilmar Mendes likened the state to abandonment and proximity to organized crime, while Alexandre de Moraes and Flávio Dino highlighted the history of investigated and imprisoned officials, including the Marielle case and former governors’ arrests. The judgment reflects concern over political instability and the need for institutional clarity.

item.title: Regulamentação de aplicativos: governo fecha posição contra nova versão de projeto, mas parte da base deve votar a favor
item.description: The Lula government has closed its position against the substitute bill regulating app-based work proposed by Deputy Augusto Coutinho, arguing that the text undermines the key points of the working group led by Guilherme Boulos, despite being seen as an improvement over the status quo by parts of the governing coalition and the platforms. The bill offers two remuneration options: R$ 8.50 for up to 3 km (by motorcycle/car) or 4 km (on foot/bicycle), or an hourly wage not lower than that of two minimum wages. Lula stresses the importance of fulfilling his electoral promise to guarantee rights for Brazil’s 1.7 million app-based workers in 2024.

item.title: Alcolumbre convoca sessão do Congresso que pode derrubar veto de Lula ao PL da Dosimetria
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) has called a joint session of Congress for April 30 to consider overturning President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's (PT) veto on the Dosimetry Bill, which addresses salary adjustments for public servants. Lawmakers will vote to either uphold or reject the veto, a decision that could affect the federal budget and Executive-Legislative relations.

item.title: Fux defende Rio após “descrédito generalizado” e cita Master, INSS e Lava Jato
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Luiz Fux defended Rio de Janeiro during the trial over the model for the 'stopgap mandate' elections, arguing that accountability for public issues should not be limited to the state. He criticized the 'generalized discredit' against Rio and cited cases such as INSS, Operation Car Wash (Lava Jato), and the company Master as examples of systemic failures not exclusive to Rio.

item.title: Alcolumbre marca sessão que pode derrubar o veto de Lula ao PL da Dosimetria
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) has scheduled a joint session of Congress for April 30 to consider President Lula’s veto of the Dosimetria Bill, which would reduce sentences for January 8 coup plotters, including Jair Bolsonaro. Overturning the veto requires an absolute majority in each chamber, a move Alcolumbre previously avoided amid other political crises but now supports under pressure from Bolsonarist lawmakers.

item.title: Alcolumbre convoca para 30 de abril análise de veto ao PL da Dosimetria
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre has called a joint congressional session for April 30 to review President Lula's full veto of the Dosimetry Bill, which seeks to reduce sentences for those convicted of the January 8 attacks. If the veto is overturned, the bill would take effect, potentially benefiting figures like Jair Bolsonaro. Critics argue it amounts to total amnesty, while supporters claim it only seeks proportionality in sentencing.

item.title: Alcolumbre convoca sessão para Congresso votar veto de Lula ao PL da Dosimetria
item.description: Congress President Senator Davi Alcolumbre has convened a joint session of the Chamber and Senate for April 30, with the sole agenda item being President Lula’s veto of the Dosimetry Bill. The vote was requested by the opposition following Lula’s January veto. The bill regulates ionizing radiation dosimetry in workplaces.

item.title: Indicado ao STF, Jorge Messias será sabatinado em 29 de abril
item.description: Senator Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA) announced that the hearing for Jorge Messias, the Attorney General of the Union nominated to the Supreme Federal Court, will take place on April 29 in the Senate. Weverton, appointed as rapporteur, said he will issue a favorable opinion, stating that Messias meets constitutional requirements of 'notable legal knowledge and impeccable reputation'. The report reading is scheduled for April 15, with the hearing in the CCJ in the morning and a plenary vote later.

item.title: Sabatina de Jorge Messias para vaga no STF será dia 29 de abril
item.description: The sabatina of Attorney General Jorge Messias for a vacancy on the Supreme Federal Court (STF) is scheduled for April 29 in the morning, as announced by rapporteur Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA). Following the sabatina, the Senate plenary will vote on his nomination the same day. Rocha stated his report will be favorable, noting Messias meets all requirements, including exceptional legal knowledge and impeccable reputation.

item.title: Dino pede vista em julgamento sobre eleições no Rio de Janeiro, mas ministros adiantam voto
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino requested a pause (vista) in the trial regarding the interim governorship election in Rio de Janeiro, halting proceedings despite Ministers André Mendonça and Kassio Nunes Marques advancing their votes in favor of indirect elections. The current vote stands at 2-1 for indirect elections by state deputies, while injunctions keep Judge Ricardo Couto as acting governor until the STF concludes the case.

item.title: Governo Lula publica protocolo para reforçar investigações de crimes contra jornalistas
item.description: The government of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva published a National Investigation Protocol for Crimes Against Journalists, aiming to strengthen investigative mechanisms and prevent violence against press professionals. Announced on April 9, 2026, the measure seeks to enhance protection and accountability in cases of threats, assaults, and killings of journalists across Brazil.

item.title: Alcolumbre marca para o próximo dia 30 análise ao veto do PL da Dosimetria, que reduz pena de Bolsonaro
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre has scheduled April 30 for the congressional analysis of President Lula's veto on the Dosimetry Bill, which seeks to reduce the sentence of Jair Bolsonaro and others involved in the January 8 attacks. The bill, passed by Congress in late 2024, was fully vetoed by Lula on January 8. Overriding the veto requires 257 votes in the Chamber of Deputies and 41 in the Senate.

item.title: Alcolumbre convoca para o dia 30 de abril sessão do Congresso para analisar veto ao PL da Dosimetria
item.description: Congress President Davi Alcolumbre has called a joint session for April 30 to review President Lula’s veto of the Dosimetria bill, which seeks to reduce sentences for those convicted in the January 8 attacks. Overturning the veto would require 257 votes in the Chamber and 41 in the Senate, potentially benefiting around 280 individuals, including Jair Bolsonaro, whose transition to semi-open regime could be moved from 2033 to approximately 2027. Lula’s veto, issued on January 8, 2024, aims to preserve accountability for the anti-democratic acts, despite the possibility of congressional override.

item.title: Alcolumbre convoca sessão do Congresso para votar veto de Lula a projeto que reduz penas do 8/1 e beneficia Bolsonaro
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre has called a joint session of Congress for April 30 to review Lula’s veto of the dosimetry bill, which reduces penalties for those involved in the January 8 attacks. The move aims to prevent the session from being used to advance CPIs, such as the one targeting Banco Master, and to ease political pressure from the opposition. Lula vetoed the bill, arguing it undermines individualized sentencing and constitutes legislative overreach into judicial authority.

item.title: O impasse no TSE sobre crime de boca de urna nos stories do Instagram
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques requested a view and interrupted the TSE judgment on whether an Instagram story listing supported candidates constitutes digital 'mouth of the urn' crime. Rapporteur Minister Estela Aranha voted to acquit prefeita Ana Malacarne, arguing the post was an individual and silent expression of preference. Minister Antonio Carlos Ferreira advocated maintaining the conviction, citing the phrases 'vote certo' and 'vamos juntos' as explicit vote requests.

item.title: STF tem 2 a 1 por voto indireto no RJ; Dino pede vista
item.description: The Supreme Court is split 2-1 in favor of maintaining indirect elections for the Rio de Janeiro governorship, with Flávio Dino requesting a delay to await the TSE ruling on Cláudio Castro's ineligibility. André Mendonça anticipated his vote to side with Luiz Fux, rejecting the cassation argument and stating that the Rio PSD lacks standing to petition the Court, as Castro's resignation was aimed at disqualification for a 2026 Senate run.

item.title: Davi Alcolumbre deve enviar indicação de Messias à CCJ nesta quinta e destravar sabatina ao STF
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) is expected to submit on Thursday (9) to the Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) President Lula’s nomination of Jorge Messias to the STF, after a four-month delay. The move should clear the way for Messias’ confirmation hearing at the Supreme Federal Court.

item.title: Indicado ao STF, Messias será sabatinado no Senado em 29 de abril
item.description: Union Advocate-General Jorge Messias, nominated by Lula for the STF, will be questioned by the Senate’s Constitution and Justice Committee on April 29. The hearing, lasting up to eight hours, will allow all 81 senators to ask questions, followed by secret votes in the committee and plenary, requiring an absolute majority of 41 votes for approval. The nomination, settled since November, was finalized after political negotiations, with Senator Rodrigo Pacheco (PSB-MG) playing a key role in overcoming Senate resistance.

item.title: Dino pede vista e interrompe julgamento sobre eleições no Rio
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino requested additional time (vista) to review the case determining how the new governor of Rio de Janeiro will be chosen following Cláudio Castro's (PL) departure from office. The hearing, which began on Wednesday, April 8, resumed on Thursday, April 9, but was suspended to allow further analysis.

item.title: Lula sanciona leis para fortalecer combate à violência contra mulheres
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed three laws to strengthen the fight against violence against women, including electronic monitoring of aggressors, expansion of protective measures, and increased penalties for femicide. The measures aim to provide greater protection to victims and greater accountability for perpetrators.

item.title: Moraes veta pedido de Lindbergh para que Moro fosse investigado por fala
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes denied a request by federal deputy Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) to investigate Senator Sergio Moro (PL-PR) over statements questioning the legitimacy of the 2022 elections. The request followed Moro's claims that electronic voting machines could have been fraudulent, but Moraes found insufficient grounds to open an inquiry. The decision underscores the STF's stance on protecting political speech, even when controversial, under freedom of expression.

item.title: Janja corrige Lula durante sanção de leis de proteção à mulher
item.description: First Lady Janja Lula da Silva corrected President Lula during a speech at the Planalto Palace, pointing out that the 5,000 arrests for gender-based violence were of men, not people in general. Lula repeated the corrected statement. The incident occurs amid a history of controversial remarks by the president, including statements deemed misogynistic, and reflects a media strategy by Secom that increased his exposure and risk of gaffes.

item.title: Fux rebate 'descrédito' de ministros com o Rio e diz que políticos que vão para o inferno estarão acompanhados de 'altas autoridades'
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Luiz Fux pushed back against colleagues' criticism of Rio de Janeiro's political situation, stating there is 'generalized discredit' toward the state and that if Rio politicians go to hell, they will be accompanied by 'high authorities'. He argued that scandals are not concentrated in Rio, citing the Banco Master case as an example of broader institutional issues.

item.title: Governo estuda liberar R$ 7 bi do FGTS para endividados, mas Caixa não confirma valor
item.description: The government is studying the release of R$ 7 billion from the FGTS that was not withdrawn by workers due to an incomplete disbursement in the 2025 birthday-savings withdrawals, according to the Ministry of Labor. Caixa Econômica Federal did not confirm the amount, stating it strictly follows legislation and the FGTS Curatorial Board’s directives. Approximately 10 million workers could benefit from the release of this remaining amount.

item.title: André Mendonça vai decidir se manda Congresso ressuscitar PL da Dosimetria
item.description: Supreme Court Justice André Mendonça has been assigned as rapporteur in a lawsuit filed by ASFAV seeking to compel the National Congress to reconsider presidential vetoes on the Dosimetry Bill. Congress President Davi Alcolumbre indicated plans to meet with Chamber President Hugo Motta to schedule a vote on overturning Lula’s full veto of the bill, which was approved by the Senate in December. The suit alleges legislative omission by lawmakers regarding the radiation dosimetry measure.

item.title: Aliados de Lula buscam momento ideal para começar a desgastar Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Lula’s allies say they are waiting for the right moment to begin damaging Flávio Bolsonaro’s image, the PL’s presidential candidate, despite his stronger-than-expected polling performance. They believe that since over half of voters could still change their minds, timing the attack strategically is crucial to prevent a recovery by the opposition. With Lula and Flávio technically tied in recent polls, the ruling coalition aims to weaken the rival carefully to avoid a repeat of the emotionally charged 2022 election outcome.

item.title: “É mais fácil tirar voto do Flávio que do Lula”, afirma Kassab
item.description: Gilberto Kassab, president of the PSD, stated that it is easier to take votes from Flávio Bolsonaro than from Lula due to the latter's stronger voter loyalty and the fluidity of the right-wing electorate, often driven by opposition to the other side. He positioned Goiás Governor Ronaldo Caiado as a competitive alternative to attract conservatives dissatisfied with polarization, emphasizing that the 2026 electoral landscape is still forming and depends on the consolidation of candidacies and alliances.

item.title: Mendonça se preocupa com “deslegitimação” do TSE
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes expressed concern over the potential delegitimization of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) amid a conflict between the two courts regarding the rules for Rio de Janeiro's supplementary gubernatorial election. The dispute centers on whether the interim mandate should be decided by direct popular vote or indirect vote by the state Legislative Assembly. The issue is currently under review by the Supreme Court, which is assessing the constitutionality of existing electoral rules.

item.title: Eleição e bolso: o conceito de 'affordability' que explica por que bons números da economia não garantem votos; ouça 'O Assunto'
item.description: Despite positive macroeconomic indicators in Brazil, many citizens do not feel an improvement in their quality of life due to the concept of 'affordability,' which measures the real ability to cope with the cost of living. Qualitative research identifies three key factors: excessive indebtedness (overdraft, credit cards, consigned loans), consumption frustration (inability to access well-being-associated goods like 'picanha e cerveja'), and hidden spending on online betting (bets), which silently erode household income without clear awareness.

item.title: Lula nomeia 1ª mulher para comandar agência de assistência rural
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva appointed agronomist engineer Loroana Santana as the first woman to lead Anater, the National Agency for Technical Assistance and Rural Extension, linked to the Ministry of Agrarian Development and Family Farming. The appointment, published in the Official Gazette on April 9, 2026, also highlights Fernanda Machiaveli's historic role as the first woman to head the ministry.

item.title: CCJ marca sabatina de Messias para 29 de abril, e relator adianta voto favorável
item.description: The Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee (CCJ) has scheduled the hearing for Jorge Messias, President Lula's nominee for the Supreme Federal Court (STF), for April 29, with the rapporteur already indicating a favorable vote. On the same date, the CCJ and the plenary are expected to vote on the nomination, as outlined by the committee's president. This accelerates the process of filling the vacancy on Brazil's highest court.

item.title: O que o Planalto espera da sabatina de Messias
item.description: Planalto officials are confident that Jorge Messias, Lula’s nominee to the STF, will be approved by the Senate’s CCJ in a hearing scheduled for April 29. They believe he has sufficient support to pass both the committee and the full plenary vote, potentially exceeding Flávio Dino’s 47 votes in his hearing. This optimism is bolstered by Senate President Davi Alcolumbre’s signal not to delay the process and the anticipated reduction in opposition if Rodrigo Pacheco runs for governor of Minas Gerais.

item.title: Alcolumbre marca sabatina de Jorge Messias na CCJ do Senado
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre has scheduled the confirmation hearing for Jorge Messias before the Constitution and Justice Committee on April 29, with rapporteur Weverton Rocha already indicating a favorable vote. The nomination of the current Attorney General of the Union to the Supreme Federal Court, made by Lula after a four-month vacancy, will proceed to a secret plenary vote the same day, requiring at least 41 votes for approval. Despite lacking initial vote guarantees, the government maintained its strategy to advance the process to avoid proximity with the electoral calendar, and historically the Senate rarely rejects Supreme Court nominees.

item.title: CCJ do Senado marca para 29/4 sabatina de Messias, indicado ao STF
item.description: The hearing for Jorge Messias, nominated to the STF by President Lula, is scheduled for April 29 in the Senate’s CCJ, with the report reading set for April 15. The nomination was submitted to the Senate on April 1, 2026, after delays due to political wear, as Senate President Davi Alcolumbre had preferred Senator Rodrigo Pacheco for the vacancy. Messias, current Attorney General of the Union, has dined with senators and Zanin to secure support for his approval.
